title: Research on Sample Imbalanced Data Augmentation Algorithm Based on Gradient Patch SMOTE
abstract: Classification of imbalanced data poses a significant challenge in the field of machine learning and data mining, as standard classifiers tend to bias toward the majority class and exhibit poor generalization on the minority class. Although the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) is widely used to mitigate this issue, its blind interpolation mechanism often introduces noise and blurs decision boundaries, especially in complex topological manifolds. To address these limitations, this paper proposes an innovative data augmentation algorithm named Gradient Patch SMOTE (GP-SMOTE). The core philosophy of GP-SMOTE is to generate patch samples locally and exclusively within "gradient anomaly regions." By constructing a potential energy field in the feature space, the algorithm defines a spatial gradient function based on Gaussian kernel density to capture the rate of change in class distribution. Regions characterized by severe class overlap or density abruptness are identified as gradient anomaly areas through a statistical threshold mechanism. Instead of global over-sampling, GP-SMOTE treats these areas as information gaps and applies localized "patches" by generating synthetic samples. Furthermore, a gradient-guided adjustment term is integrated into the interpolation logic to ensure that the synthetic samples conform closely to the underlying manifold structure without invading the majority class space. The proposed GP-SMOTE algorithm provides a more robust and precise data augmentation strategy for handling complex, imbalanced datasets by effectively reinforcing critical decision boundaries while avoiding redundant data generation.

title: An Imbalance Data Augmentation Algorithm Based on Feature Causality Shuffle and SMOTE (FCS-SMOTE)
abstract: Class imbalance is a fundamental bottleneck that restricts the classification performance of machine learning models. Although the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) is widely used to address this issue, it primarily relies on local geometric proximity in the feature space and overlooks the underlying causal relationships among features. Consequently, traditional SMOTE is prone to generating "hallucinated samples" that violate real-world physical or logical constraints. To resolve this limitation, this paper proposes a novel data augmentation algorithm named Feature Causality Shuffle SMOTE (FCS-SMOTE). The proposed method integrates causal mechanism constraints into the over-sampling process. First, a directed acyclic graph (DAG) is learned from the data to discover the causal dependencies and establish a topological execution order of the features. Second, a conditional feature shuffling mechanism is introduced to randomly permute the root features across minority samples, while conditionally swapping non-root features only within an equivalent causal background to maintain the conditional probability distributions. Finally, a causal-guided conditional interpolation is performed on the shuffled samples, where the interpolation coefficients of downstream features are bound to or weighted by their corresponding parent nodes to preserve structural deterministic functions. By combining structural feature recombination with conditional geometric interpolation, FCS-SMOTE effectively expands the diversity of the minority class while ensuring that the synthesized samples strictly conform to the underlying causal mechanisms. This approach prevents the generation of logically invalid data and enhances the generalization boundaries for subsequent classifiers.

title: Utility-Scale Quantum Computational Chemistry
abstract: Chemistry and materials science are widely regarded as leading application fields for quantum hardware. While the dream of unlocking unprecedented simulation capabilities remains compelling, quantum algorithm development must adapt to the evolving constraints of the emerging quantum hardware in order to accomplish any advantage for the computational chemistry practice. At the same time, the continuous advancement of classical wavefunction-theory methods narrows the window for a broad quantum advantage. Here, we explore potential benefits of quantum computation from the broader perspective of utility-scale applications. We argue that quantum algorithms need not only enable accurate calculations for a few challenging, that is, strongly correlated, molecular structures, which might be hard to describe with traditional methods. Instead, they must also support the practical integration of quantum-accelerated computations into high-throughput pipelines for routine calculations on arbitrary molecules, ultimately delivering a tangible value to society.

evidence.title: Utility-Scale Quantum Computational Chemistry
evidence.abstract: Chemistry and materials science are widely regarded as leading application fields for quantum hardware. While the dream of unlocking unprecedented simulation capabilities remains compelling, quantum algorithm development must adapt to the evolving constraints of the emerging quantum hardware in order to accomplish any advantage for the computational chemistry practice. At the same time, the continuous advancement of classical wavefunction-theory methods narrows the window for a broad quantum advantage. Here, we explore potential benefits of quantum computation from the broader perspective of utility-scale applications. We argue that quantum algorithms need not only enable accurate calculations for a few challenging, that is, strongly correlated, molecular structures, which might be hard to describe with traditional methods. Instead, they must also support the practical integration of quantum-accelerated computations into high-throughput pipelines for routine calculations on arbitrary molecules, ultimately delivering a tangible value to society.

title: Lattice-based cryptography and post-quantum security: Algebraic number theory in the design of quantum-resistant cryptographic schemes
abstract: Background: The imminent threat posed by cryptographically relevant quantum computers to classical public-key infrastructure specifically RSA and Elliptic-Curve Cryptography (ECC), whose security rests on the conjectured computational intractability of integer factorisation and the discrete logarithm problem respectively has propelled lattice-based cryptography to the centre of global post-quantum standardisation efforts. On 13 August 2024, the United States National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) published three landmark Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS): FIPS 203 (ML-KEM, derived from CRYSTALS-Kyber), FIPS 204 (ML-DSA, derived from CRYSTALS-Dilithium), and FIPS 205 (SLH-DSA, derived from SPHINCS+), with FIPS 206 (FN-DSA, derived from FALCON) in advanced draft. The first three of these standards rest on algebraic structures intimately connected to classical number theory: polynomial rings over integer quotients, cyclotomic fields, and the algebraic geometry of ideal lattices in rings of integers of number fields. Objectives: This article provides: (1) a rigorous mathematical exposition of the lattice problems underpinning NIST’s post-quantum standards, specifically the Learning With Errors (LWE), Ring-LWE (RLWE), Module-LWE (MLWE), Short Integer Solution (SIS), and NTRU problems, and their connections to algebraic number theory; (2) a comparative performance analysis of NIST-standardised lattice-based algorithms against classical RSA and ECC benchmarks; (3) a security analysis examining known classical and quantum attacks on each hard problem; (4) a comparative evaluation of the four NIST-selected algorithms across key size, signature size, and computational benchmarks; and (5) a strategic assessment of the migration challenges facing deployed cryptographic infrastructure. Methods: The study synthesises peer-reviewed literature, NIST official standards documentation (FIPS 203, 204, 205, and draft FIPS 206), and independently published performance benchmarks published between June 2024 and June 2026. Mathematical security analysis is grounded in the worst-case to average-case reductions established by Regev (2005) for LWE and by Lyubashevsky, Peikert, and Regev (2013) [11, 18] for Ring-LWE. Performance data are drawn from Garani (2024) [8], the ARM Cortex-M0+ benchmarking study of Ratnayaka and Fischer (2026) [4], and the cross-platform evaluation by Alzahrani et al. (2025) [2]. Results: NIST’s three August 2024 standards establish a comprehensive lattice-based post-quantum portfolio. ML-KEM-768 produces a 1,184-byte public key and 1,088-byte ciphertext, achieving IND-CCA2 security under the MLWE assumption at NIST Level 3 (AES-192 equivalent). ML-DSA-65 produces 1,952-byte public keys and 3,309-byte signatures under the Module-LWE and Module-SIS assumptions at Level 3. FN-DSA-512 (FALCON, draft FIPS 206) produces 897-byte public keys and 666-byte signatures under the NTRU assumption, offering the most compact lattice-based signatures. Performance benchmarks on an Intel Core i7-12700K (3.6 GHz) confirm that ML-KEM key generation is orders of magnitude faster than RSA-3072 key generation. The algebraic structure of cyclotomic polynomial rings ∑₂ⁿ = Z[x]/(x^n + 1) is central to the efficiency of all three lattice-based NIST standards. Conclusion: Lattice-based cryptography, grounded in the algebraic number theory of ideal lattices over cyclotomic fields, provides the most comprehensive and mathematically well-founded response to the quantum computational threat. The August 2024 NIST standardisation of ML-KEM, ML-DSA, and SLH-DSA represents a landmark in cryptographic history, and the imminent finalisation of FN-DSA will complete the post-quantum toolbox. Organisations should prioritise immediate migration planning, leveraging hybrid classical-quantum schemes during transition, with full transition to NIST post-quantum standards recommended by 2030 per NSA and CISA guidance.

title: Explaining Classification Through Global Sufficient Reasons and its Complexity
abstract: In recent years, explainable AI has become a major focus of research, driven by the need to better understand how AI systems arrive at their decisions in order to ensure trust and effective deployment. A central challenge in this field is the explanation of classifiers. Existing approaches typically distinguish between local explanations, which account for a classifier’s decision on an individual input, and global explanations, which aim to characterize the classifier’s behavior as a whole, independent of any particular input. This work concentrates on global explanations and characterizes classification decisions through "maximal" sufficient conditions that, when satisfied, guarantee that the classifier assigns the desired class to any input. We present a detailed analysis of the computational complexity of key problems in this setting across several important families of classifiers considered in the literature.

title: The Cognitive Architecture of Management in the Age of Generative AI: Neurophysiological Transitions, Metacognitive Shifts, and the Professional Evolution from Creator to Editor
abstract: Abstract The integration of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) into the executive suite represents one of the most profound shifts in human cognition since the industrialization of information. As of 2026, organizational adoption of Large Language Models (LLMs) has reached a critical threshold, with approximately 78% of global enterprises incorporating these tools into at least one primary managerial function. 1 This transition is largely driven by a perceived “performance multiplier” effect, where managers report spending 35% to 45% less time on repetitive tasks such as documentation, report drafting, and information synthesis. 1 However, the efficiency gains observed in the short term mask a complex restructuring of the neural and metacognitive frameworks that underpin strategic judgment. The transition from ‘creator’—where the individual is the primary source of ideation and structural logic—to ‘editor’— where the individual serves as a supervisor of algorithmic output—is not merely a change in workflow but a fundamental reconfiguration of the human brain’s engagement with professional challenges. 2

title: تأثير تقنيات الذكاء الاصطناعي في تحسين الاداء التسويقي وارتباط العملاء الكترونيا الدور الوسيط للابتكار التسويقي دراسة تطبيقية علي عملاء الشركة المصرية للاتصالات بمحافظة الدقهلية
authors: د. سنية محمد أحمد سليمان سبع
abstract: تهدف الدراسة الحالية إلى قياس الدور الوسيط للابتكار التسويقي في العلاقة بين تقنيات الذكاء الاصطناعي وتحسين الأداء التسويقي وارتباط العملاء إلكترونيًا، بالتطبيق على عملاء الشركة المصرية للاتصالات بمحافظة الدقهلية. اعتمدت الدراسة على استبيان موجه لعينة مكونة من (291) عميلًا، تم اختيارهم باستخدام أسلوب العينة العشوائية المنتظمة. تم تحليل البيانات باستخدام برنامجي ( (SPSS V26 و(AMOS V26) لاختبار فروض الدراسة.توصلت النتائج إلى وجود علاقة ارتباط معنوية بين متغيرات الدراسة، حيث تبين أن تقنيات الذكاء الاصطناعي تؤثر بشكل إيجابي على تحسين الأداء التسويقي وأبعاد ارتباط العملاء إلكترونيًا. كما أظهرت النتائج وجود تأثير معنوي لتقنيات الذكاء الاصطناعي على أبعاد الابتكار التسويقي. وكشفت الدراسة أيضًا أن الابتكار التسويقي يلعب دورًا وسيطًا هامًا في تعزيز تأثير تقنيات الذكاء الاصطناعي على تحسين الأداء التسويقي وارتباط العملاء إلكترونيًا. بالإضافة إلى ذلك، أظهرت النتائج وجود اختلافات معنوية بين آراء العملاء تجاه متغيرات الدراسة تبعًا للاختلافات الديموغرافية والتنظيمية.في ضوء هذه النتائج، أوصت الدراسة بضرورة تعزيز استثمارات الشركة في تقنيات الذكاء الاصطناعي لتطوير الأداء التسويقي، وتنفيذ برامج ابتكارية تعزز تفاعل العملاء إلكترونيًا، بالإضافة إلى تحسين بيئة العمل بما يدعم الابتكار المستدام في العمليات التسويقية. كما أوصت الدراسة بتطوير أدوات قياس لمتابعة رضا العملاء وتعزيز الشفافية في تقديم الخدمات.الكلمات المفتاحية: الذكاء الاصطناعي، الابتكار التسويقي، الأداء التسويقي، ارتباط العملاء إلكترونيًا.

title: An algorithm for generating cryptographically stable S-box optimized for programmable logic integrated circuits
abstract: Cryptographic primitives implemented on Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) have a number of advantages over their software counterparts; they are more efficient in terms of performance and energy consumption. At the same time, for implementation on FPGAs, it is important to have a compact representation of cryptographic primitive elements such as substitution tables (S-boxes). This paper presents a cryptographically strong S-box that is compact in its implementation on FPGAs. Based on the algorithm for generating bent functions using wavelet transform, an algorithm for constructing S-boxes has been developed. The nonlinearity, differential uniformity, avalanche effect, and Bit Independence Criterion (BIC) of the S-boxes generated by the developed algorithm are calculated. Diagrams have been constructed showing the distribution of S-boxes by nonlinearity and differential uniformity values for different values of the algorithm input data. A comparison was made of the cryptographic properties of the generated S-boxes and the S-boxes used in the American Advanced Encryption Standard symmetric encryption standard and the Russian Kuznechik cipher. The avalanche effect of the Streebog hash function was analyzed when using its S-box and the S-box generated by the developed algorithm, and a comparison of FPGA resource utilization was performed. The best results in terms of nonlinearity, differential uniformity, avalanche effect, and BIC are achieved by S-boxes consisting of bent functions that have no terms higher than degree two (quadratic bent functions) in algebraic normal form. In terms of cryptographic properties, the S-boxes generated by the developed algorithm are superior to or not inferior to existing ones, but they are not bijective, which narrows their field of application. The avalanche effect of the hash function with its original S-box and the S-box generated by the developed algorithm do not differ. Analysis of the results of the synthesis of hash function implementations showed that the use of the developed S-box allows saving about 1000 Look Up Tables on the FPGA. The S-boxes presented in this work are not inferior to existing ones in terms of cryptographic properties, or surpass them. The developed S-boxes are more compact than existing ones in hardware implementation on FPGAs, but they are not bijective, which makes their use most appropriate and natural in irreversible cryptographic primitives implemented on resource-limited embedded systems.

title: Integrated transceiver chip for metropolitan WDM quantum key distributions
abstract: The realization of large-scale, practical quantum key distribution (QKD) networks relies on the development of scalable architectures and integrated hardware. We demonstrate a metropolitan wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) QKD network based on hybrid-integrated quantum node transceiver chips that integrate both transmitter and receiver functionalities, including high-speed pulse modulation, decoy-state modulation, tunable attenuation, time-bin encoding, and decoding. The packaged module offers a wavelength tuning range exceeding 85 nm, with its silicon photonic Mach–Zehnder modulator (MZM) achieving a single-photon equivalent dynamic extinction ratio (SP-EDER) of over 20 dB across the entire tuning range at a 1.25 GHz pulse repetition rate. In combination with a simple 1.25 GHz clocked integrated time-bin QKD system, we generate secret keys at a rate of 865.4 kbps over a channel with 9.08 dB of fixed attenuation and at a rate of 168.2 kbps over a distance of 80 km at 1550.12 nm. Our work demonstrates an integrated WDM QKD network capable of supporting scalable and cost-effective metropolitan quantum-secure communications.

title: Research on the identification of surface heat flux density of disc brakes based on the improved artificial lemming algorithm
abstract: Abstract Under high-speed braking conditions, identifying transient heat flux density in brake discs is essential for thermal analysis and structural optimization, but remains a challenging inverse heat conduction problem. To address this issue, an improved artificial lemming algorithm (IALA) is proposed for heat flux identification using limited temperature measurements. The proposed method incorporates three strategies: Tent chaotic initialization to enhance population diversity, a linearly decreasing inertia weight to balance exploration and exploitation, and an adaptive Lévy flight mechanism to prevent premature convergence. The inverse problem is formulated as a parameter optimization task by minimizing the discrepancy between measured and calculated temperatures. Experimental results show that IALA achieves an average relative error of 1.86%, outperforming artificial lemming algorithm, grey wolf optimizer, and particle swarm optimization. Furthermore, the robustness of the proposed method with respect to different heat flux boundary conditions, braking duration, number of measurement points, and temperature measurement noise is systematically investigated. The proposed method provides an effective tool for brake thermal analysis and supports engineering design optimization.

title: Joint inference of radar usage and working mode knowledge graph via attention screening and distance measurement
abstract: Accurate inference of multifunction radar usage and working modes is vital for electronic warfare situational awareness. However, with the development of multi-functional radar technology, the increasing complexity in radar parameters makes inference challenging. Knowledge graphs effectively integrate and represent structured knowledge, enabling the discovery of intrinsic relationships. Traditional distance-based knowledge embedding models struggle with complex structures like one-to-many mappings, while neural models often overlook the spatial distance relationships between vectors. To overcome these limitations, we propose ASAD—a joint reasoning model that integrates attention screening and distance measurement. First, we construct a radar knowledge graph to represent semantic information about radar usage and working modes. Then, an attention mechanism filters noisy or irrelevant triples to improve reasoning quality. Finally, a distance-based embedding captures complex semantic relationships and enables robust joint inference. We evaluate ASAD on a dataset containing five radar usages and fifteen working modes under varying triple-missing rates and signal-to-noise ratios. Experimental results show ASAD significantly outperforms traditional models in accuracy and robustness. Despite missing data or noise, ASAD maintains stable performance, demonstrating its effectiveness for radar knowledge inference tasks.

title: How to manage the intersection of generative AI, intellectual property
abstract: CLEARWATER BEACH, Fla. — When it comes to generative artificial intelligence, higher education institutions have too narrowly focused on risk management, trying to define and ensure the acceptable, responsible use of AI, according to Jacob Rooksby, J.D., Ph.D., Dean, Gonzaga University School of Law, and IP Optimization Strategist with Fig. 1 Patents, PLLC. While speaking at Stetson University's National Conference on Law and Higher Education, he said it's time for colleges and universities to expand their scope by developing AI‐related strategies for supporting institutional values, educational purpose, and authenticity, as well as concerns about ownership, governance, and the future.

title: Nexus: Depth-Adaptive KV-Cache Splicing and Retrieval-Decoupled Tool Routing for Agentic LLMs on Unified Memory
abstract: Agentic large language models (LLMs) on the Model Context Protocol (MCP) re-encode verbose tool schemas every turn, so prefill - quadratic in sequence length - dominates time-to-first-token (TTFT) as the tool registry grows. Nexus's primary lever is to decouple routing from the schema-prefill cost: an INT8 semantic lookaside buffer (SLB) with a calibrated cross-encoder margin gate selects tools by retrieval, and arguments are generated over a compressed textual signature (median 19 tokens) rather than over spliced key/value (KV) cache. This path is depth-independent: routing accuracy stays near 89% as the registry scales to 250 tools - where a concatenate-all-schemas baseline overflows the context window entirely - and it reaches a first-argument token 1.66x sooner than a full-schema re-prefill at a ~80% main-context token saving. As a secondary, bounded lever we transplant a compiled schema KV block directly into the live context. This is fundamentally limited by rotary position embedding (RoPE) phase drift: an anchored splice is output-exact, but off-anchor placement corrupts attention, so beyond a threshold P=256 Nexus repairs the seam with a depth-adaptive suffix redecode that escalates to a full re-prefill. The resulting never-regress property is a guarantee on output fidelity (top-1 agreement, D_KL approx. 0) - not on latency, which can dip to 0.98x before converging to parity - alongside a 1.1-1.7x TTFT speedup at moderate depth that narrows to parity at deep context. Two negative results bound the design: the off-anchor RoPE fidelity boundary, and the failure of a reference-free drift gate to predict drift (Spearman rho = 0.193). All measurements are from one model tuple (Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct Q4_K_M) on Apple-silicon unified memory; the qualitative boundaries generalize, while the quantitative envelope is tuple-specific.

title: A Fuzzy Sphere Journey in Critical Phenomena
abstract: This review discusses the recently proposed fuzzy sphere regularization for studying 2+1D critical phenomena, particularly three-dimensional (3D) conformal field theory (CFT). The fuzzy sphere scheme not only offers remarkable efficiency in extracting extensive CFT data at low computational cost but also reveals unexpected connections among 3D CFT (critical phenomena), noncommutative geometry, and the quantum Hall effect. We introduce the fundamental ideas of fuzzy sphere regularization, emphasizing its role in demonstrating the state-operator correspondence of 3D CFTs on the S^2 times R geometry. Additionally, we review key developments in this approach across various directions and outline potential future applications.

title: QuasiMoTTo: Quasi-Monte Carlo Test-Time Scaling
abstract: Scaling inference compute, by generating many parallel attempts per problem, is a costly but reliable lever for improving language model capabilities. By default these attempts are generated independently, wasting inference compute on redundant solutions. This waste seems unavoidable. After all, independence is what makes parallel sampling trivial to scale. However, this tradeoff is not fundamental: there is a rich design space of samplers that generate correlated but exact samples entirely in parallel. We explore this design space as an avenue for improving sample efficiency in scaling inference compute and reinforcement learning (RL). Concretely, we introduce QuasiMoTTo, which uses correlated samples as a drop-in replacement for i.i.d. samples. To generate these samples, QuasiMoTTo uses a reparameterization of autoregressive sampling as inverse-CDF sampling and draws the underlying uniforms with quasi-Monte Carlo (QMC); because QMC spreads the uniforms out more evenly than i.i.d., the resulting samples cover the output space with far less redundancy. Even though the batch is correlated, each sample is marginally distributed according to the language model, so we can use the batch for policy-gradient training. Our empirical analysis focuses on understanding how efficiently QuasiMoTTo can turn compute into performance. To evaluate correlated samplers, whose dependence breaks standard pass@k estimators, we first develop an unbiased bootstrap estimator. Across four reasoning benchmarks, QuasiMoTTo matches i.i.d. pass@k accuracy with 25-47% fewer samples. Strikingly, QuasiMoTTo often saturates an upper bound on pass@k that holds for any marginal-preserving sampler. We also apply QuasiMoTTo to policy-gradient RL (GRPO) where it matches i.i.d. performance with 50% fewer training steps. These gains come from higher coverage, which yields a stronger learning signal per batch.

title: Learning to Watch: Active Video Anomaly Understanding via Interleaved Policy Optimization
abstract: Video anomaly understanding (VAU) relies on sparse, context-dependent cues. However, existing passive paradigms suffer from observational aliasing, where static sampling fails to disambiguate semantically distinct events. To overcome this, we propose $Anom\text{-}π$, a closed-loop framework that reconceptualizes video understanding as an active sequential decision-making process within a dynamic environment. Inspired by human video-reviewing behavior, this framework unifies internal cognitive reasoning and strategic evidence acquisition into an interleaved policy, utilizing temporal atomic operators such as local backtracking, temporal expansion, and fine-grained sampling to endow the model with perceptual proactivity. To learn such complex interaction strategies under video-level weak supervision, we design Interactive Direct Preference Optimization (iDPO) to achieve trajectory-level policy alignment, guided by an Active Evidence Inquiry (AEI) utility that balances task success, informative evidence acquisition, and interaction cost. This approach enables the agent to learn to actively disambiguate hypotheses while suppressing redundant exploration. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our framework, with only 2B parameters, achieves highly competitive performance, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art large-scale VAU models in complex scenarios.

title: A Multi-Model Metric-Based Selection Framework for Abstractive Text Summarization
abstract: Automatic text summarization has become increasingly important due to the rapid growth of digital textual information. This paper presents a Multi-Model Summarization Framework designed to improve the robustness and quality of abstractive text summarization. Relying on a single model often leads to inconsistent summarization quality across articles with varying structures and topics. To address this limitation, the proposed framework integrates multiple fine-tuned transformer-based summarization models and introduces a metric-based selection mechanism. In this framework, each model independently generates a candidate summary for the same input article. The generated summaries are then evaluated using automatic evaluation metrics that capture both lexical similarity and semantic relevance. Based on these scores, the framework selects the highest-quality summary as the final output. The models are fine-tuned and evaluated on the widely used CNN/DailyMail news summarization dataset. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves the highest BERTScore among all compared methods with a score of 88.63%. It also outperforms several LLMs such as GPT3-D2, Falcon-7b, and Mpt-7b, highlighting its effectiveness and robustness. These findings highlight the effectiveness of leveraging multiple transformer-based models within a metric-based selection strategy to improve the quality and robustness of automatic text summarization systems.

title: Mixture of Distributions Matters: Dynamic Sparse Attention for Efficient Video Diffusion Transformers
abstract: While Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) have achieved notable progress in video generation, this long-sequence generation task remains constrained by the quadratic complexity inherent to self-attention mechanisms, creating significant barriers to practical deployment. Although sparse attention methods attempt to address this challenge, existing approaches either rely on oversimplified static patterns or require computationally expensive sampling operations to achieve dynamic sparsity, resulting in inaccurate pattern predictions and degraded generation quality. To overcome these limitations, we propose a \textbf{M}ixture-\textbf{O}f-\textbf{D}istribution DiT (MOD-DiT), a novel sampling-free dynamic attention framework that accurately models evolving attention patterns through a two-stage process. First, MOD-DiT leverages prior information from early denoising steps and adopts a {distributed mixing approach} to model an efficient linear approximation model, which is then used to predict mask patterns for a specific denoising interval. Second, an online block masking strategy dynamically applies these predicted masks while maintaining historical sparsity information, eliminating the need for repetitive sampling operations. Extensive evaluations demonstrate consistent acceleration and quality improvements across multiple benchmarks and model architectures, validating MOD-DiT's effectiveness for efficient, high-quality video generation while overcoming the computational limitations of traditional sparse attention approaches.

title: SAMix: Calibrated and Accurate Continual Learning via Sphere-Adaptive Mixup and Neural Collapse
abstract: Abstract While most continual learning methods focus on mitigating forgetting and improving accuracy, they often overlook the critical aspect of network calibration, despite its importance. Neural collapse, a phenomenon where last-layer features collapse to their class means, has demonstrated advantages in continual learning by reducing feature-classifier misalignment. Few works aim to improve the calibration of continual models for more reliable predictions. Our work goes a step further by proposing a novel method that not only enhances calibration but also improves performance by reducing overconfidence, mitigating forgetting, and increasing accuracy. We introduce Sphere-Adaptive Mixup (SAMix), an adaptive mixup strategy tailored for neural collapse-based methods. SAMix adapts the mixing process to the geometric properties of feature spaces under neural collapse, ensuring more robust regularization and alignment. Experiments show that SAMix significantly boosts performance, surpassing SOTA methods in continual learning while also improving model calibration. SAMix enhances both across-task accuracy and the broader reliability of predictions, making it a promising advancement for robust continual learning systems.

title: Intelligent Decision Support Framework for Distribution Network Maintenance Based on Knowledge-graph-based Retrieval-augmented Generation and Large Language Models
abstract: ObjectiveDistribution network maintenance (DNM) decision-making currently relies heavily on manual scheduling and experiential judgment, resulting in inefficient data integration, delayed information processing, and subjective bias. Although general-purpose large language models (LLMs) demonstrate strong semantic capabilities, they lack sufficient domain-specific knowledge and frequently generate hallucinations when applied to specialized maintenance scenarios. Existing retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) approaches, which rely on flat text-chunk retrieval, fail to capture the complex hierarchical structures and causal relationships embedded in power maintenance documents, including equipment fault trees, operational procedure dependencies, and cross-referenced industry standards. To address these limitations, this study proposes an intelligent DNM decision support framework that integrates knowledge graph (KG)-based retrieval-augmented generation with LLMs, termed KRAG-LLM-DM.MethodsThe KRAG-LLM-DM framework comprises several interconnected stages. Maintenance-related documents, including research literature, industry standards, and operational procedures in PDF format, are first converted into UTF-8-encoded plain text. The documents are then segmented into text chunks with configurable length thresholds to facilitate subsequent vectorization and retrieval. For KG construction, an LLM-guided, prompt-based extraction mechanism is employed. The prompt template incorporates few-shot learning, chain-of-thought reasoning, parameterized entity-type placeholders, descriptive anchoring for entity disambiguation, and structured delimiters to ensure output consistency. The LLM automatically identifies maintenance entities, such as transformers and circuit breakers, together with their semantic relationships, including causal and operational dependencies, thereby extracting both explicit and implicit knowledge from the segmented text. Relationship strength is quantified using an implicit scoring scheme to enable fine-grained relational modeling. Following entity and relationship extraction, the KG is partitioned into communities using the Leiden algorithm, which optimizes modularity through iterative node movement, partition refinement, and network aggregation. For each community, the LLM generates a hierarchical summary using a structured prompt that requires critical entity identification, compliance assessment, technical capability evaluation, impact scoring with explanatory justification, and source citation tracking. The resulting community summaries and corresponding text chunks are vectorized using one of three embedding models (Jina, Anything LLM, or Nomic) and stored in a vector database. During inference, a user query is encoded into the same embedding space, and cosine similarity retrieval is performed to identify the most relevant text chunks and community summaries. The retrieved knowledge is then combined with the original query to construct an augmented context, which is subsequently provided to the LLM for response generation.Results and DiscussionsThe framework was evaluated through a series of experiments involving knowledge base construction, ablation studies, embedding model comparisons, and decision performance benchmarking. A maintenance knowledge base was constructed from a corpus of power distribution maintenance documents. Chunk recall testing using a query on transformer maintenance procedures showed that the retrieved text fragments primarily exhibited similarity scores between 0.50 and 0.52. In the first case study, the LLM-based decision support framework without RAG was evaluated on both online cloud platforms and local offline environments. Temperature coefficient analysis showed that lower coefficients produced more structured and logically coherent responses, making them more suitable for high-reliability maintenance scenarios. Comparisons among mainstream LLMs using two maintenance planning queries showed that the proposed framework achieved recall rates of 0.719 and 0.694, representing improvements of 2.36%~13.40% over GPT-4, DeepSeek-V3, GLM-4, and Kimi. The RAG-enhanced responses explicitly referenced national standards and provided hierarchically structured answers with source attribution, whereas the baseline models often omitted domain-specific information, such as maintenance grading criteria and dynamic constraint conditions. In referential ambiguity scenarios, the framework achieved an F1-score of 0.625, marginally outperforming competing models that failed to explicitly resolve anaphoric references. The second case study investigated the influence of embedding models on the RAG-based decision support framework. Among the Jina, AnythingLLM, and Nomic embedding models, Jina demonstrated superior semantic representation of nested hierarchical structures in long power maintenance documents owing to its multi-task contrastive learning and decoupled attention mechanism. Nomic provided broader semantic representations and supported dynamic dimensionality pruning, whereas AnythingLLM exhibited information loss when processing compound semantic structures. The third case study evaluated the proposed KRAG-LLM-DM framework. The KG constructed using the proposed LLM-guided extraction method contained 18 280 nodes and 14 002 edges, with an average degree of 0.21, a modularity index of 0.953, and a network diameter of 9. Graph visualization was performed using Gephi with the ForceAtlas2 layout algorithm. Comparative analysis against keyword matching, regular expression, and SpaCy-based dependency parsing methods showed that the proposed approach achieved greater knowledge coverage and structural completeness while operating automatically without manual rule maintenance. Ablation experiments involving three complex maintenance question types yielded F1-scores of 0.726 3, 0.708 1, and 0.729 0 for the KRAG-LLM-DM framework, outperforming the LLM without RAG by 1.60%~2.63% and the standard RAG-based LLM by 1.80%~3.60%. Error analysis indicated that the KG structural constraints and hierarchical community semantics improved answer consistency and reduced logical fragmentation compared with flat RAG retrieval. Compared with parameter-matched baseline models, including Mistral, Olmo, and LLaMA, the KRAG-LLM-DM framework achieved average F1-score improvements of 3%~5% across device state identification, fault cause tracing, and maintenance recommendation tasks. Finally, an interactive decision support interface featuring knowledge provenance visualization, structured answer presentation, and multi-tab version switching was developed to facilitate human-machine collaborative decision-making.ConclusionsThe KRAG-LLM-DM framework integrates KG construction with retrieval-augmented generation to address the limitations of general-purpose LLMs in DNM decision support. The LLM-guided, prompt-based extraction mechanism enables the automated construction of structured maintenance KGs from heterogeneous unstructured text, producing 18 280 nodes and 14 002 edges without manual annotation. Hierarchical community summarization and vector-based retrieval provide semantically organized knowledge augmentation, achieving recall rates of 0.719 and 0.694 on maintenance regulation queries and grading-based planning tasks, representing improvements of 2.36%～13.40% over mainstream LLM baselines. The framework consistently outperforms both non-RAG and conventional RAG configurations on complex domain-specific queries, demonstrating the effectiveness of structured semantic constraints and multi-hop reasoning in improving the professionalism and interpretability of generated responses. Despite these advances, the coupling mechanism between LLM reasoning and graph-structured inference remains only partially interpretable, limiting the transparency of the causal reasoning process from evidence nodes to maintenance decisions. Future research should therefore focus on enhancing causal reasoning within LLM-KG integration for safety-critical power system applications.

evidence.title: Intelligent Decision Support Framework for Distribution Network Maintenance Based on Knowledge-graph-based Retrieval-augmented Generation and Large Language Models
evidence.abstract: ObjectiveDistribution network maintenance (DNM) decision-making currently relies heavily on manual scheduling and experiential judgment, resulting in inefficient data integration, delayed information processing, and subjective bias. Although general-purpose large language models (LLMs) demonstrate strong semantic capabilities, they lack sufficient domain-specific knowledge and frequently generate hallucinations when applied to specialized maintenance scenarios. Existing retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) approaches, which rely on flat text-chunk retrieval, fail to capture the complex hierarchical structures and causal relationships embedded in power maintenance documents, including equipment fault trees, operational procedure dependencies, and cross-referenced industry standards. To address these limitations, this study proposes an intelligent DNM decision support framework that integrates knowledge graph (KG)-based retrieval-augmented generation with LLMs, termed KRAG-LLM-DM.MethodsThe KRAG-LLM-DM framework comprises several interconnected stages. Maintenance-related documents, including research literature, industry standards, and operational procedures in PDF format, are first converted into UTF-8-encoded plain text. The documents are then segmented into text chunks with configurable length thresholds to facilitate subsequent vectorization and retrieval. For KG construction, an LLM-guided, prompt-based extraction mechanism is employed. The prompt template incorporates few-shot learning, chain-of-thought reasoning, parameterized entity-type placeholders, descriptive anchoring for entity disambiguation, and structured delimiters to ensure output consistency. The LLM automatically identifies maintenance entities, such as transformers and circuit breakers, together with their semantic relationships, including causal and operational dependencies, thereby extracting both explicit and implicit knowledge from the segmented text. Relationship strength is quantified using an implicit scoring scheme to enable fine-grained relational modeling. Following entity and relationship extraction, the KG is partitioned into communities using the Leiden algorithm, which optimizes modularity through iterative node movement, partition refinement, and network aggregation. For each community, the LLM generates a hierarchical summary using a structured prompt that requires critical entity identification, compliance assessment, technical capability evaluation, impact scoring with explanatory justification, and source citation tracking. The resulting community summaries and corresponding text chunks are vectorized using one of three embedding models (Jina, Anything LLM, or Nomic) and stored in a vector database. During inference, a user query is encoded into the same embedding space, and cosine similarity retrieval is performed to identify the most relevant text chunks and community summaries. The retrieved knowledge is then combined with the original query to construct an augmented context, which is subsequently provided to the LLM for response generation.Results and DiscussionsThe framework was evaluated through a series of experiments involving knowledge base construction, ablation studies, embedding model comparisons, and decision performance benchmarking. A maintenance knowledge base was constructed from a corpus of power distribution maintenance documents. Chunk recall testing using a query on transformer maintenance procedures showed that the retrieved text fragments primarily exhibited similarity scores between 0.50 and 0.52. In the first case study, the LLM-based decision support framework without RAG was evaluated on both online cloud platforms and local offline environments. Temperature coefficient analysis showed that lower coefficients produced more structured and logically coherent responses, making them more suitable for high-reliability maintenance scenarios. Comparisons among mainstream LLMs using two maintenance planning queries showed that the proposed framework achieved recall rates of 0.719 and 0.694, representing improvements of 2.36%~13.40% over GPT-4, DeepSeek-V3, GLM-4, and Kimi. The RAG-enhanced responses explicitly referenced national standards and provided hierarchically structured answers with source attribution, whereas the baseline models often omitted domain-specific information, such as maintenance grading criteria and dynamic constraint conditions. In referential ambiguity scenarios, the framework achieved an F1-score of 0.625, marginally outperforming competing models that failed to explicitly resolve anaphoric references. The second case study investigated the influence of embedding models on the RAG-based decision support framework. Among the Jina, AnythingLLM, and Nomic embedding models, Jina demonstrated superior semantic representation of nested hierarchical structures in long power maintenance documents owing to its multi-task contrastive learning and decoupled attention mechanism. Nomic provided broader semantic representations and supported dynamic dimensionality pruning, whereas AnythingLLM exhibited information loss when processing compound semantic structures. The third case study evaluated the proposed KRAG-LLM-DM framework. The KG constructed using the proposed LLM-guided extraction method contained 18 280 nodes and 14 002 edges, with an average degree of 0.21, a modularity index of 0.953, and a network diameter of 9. Graph visualization was performed using Gephi with the ForceAtlas2 layout algorithm. Comparative analysis against keyword matching, regular expression, and SpaCy-based dependency parsing methods showed that the proposed approach achieved greater knowledge coverage and structural completeness while operating automatically without manual rule maintenance. Ablation experiments involving three complex maintenance question types yielded F1-scores of 0.726 3, 0.708 1, and 0.729 0 for the KRAG-LLM-DM framework, outperforming the LLM without RAG by 1.60%~2.63% and the standard RAG-based LLM by 1.80%~3.60%. Error analysis indicated that the KG structural constraints and hierarchical community semantics improved answer consistency and reduced logical fragmentation compared with flat RAG retrieval. Compared with parameter-matched baseline models, including Mistral, Olmo, and LLaMA, the KRAG-LLM-DM framework achieved average F1-score improvements of 3%~5% across device state identification, fault cause tracing, and maintenance recommendation tasks. Finally, an interactive decision support interface featuring knowledge provenance visualization, structured answer presentation, and multi-tab version switching was developed to facilitate human-machine collaborative decision-making.ConclusionsThe KRAG-LLM-DM framework integrates KG construction with retrieval-augmented generation to address the limitations of general-purpose LLMs in DNM decision support. The LLM-guided, prompt-based extraction mechanism enables the automated construction of structured maintenance KGs from heterogeneous unstructured text, producing 18 280 nodes and 14 002 edges without manual annotation. Hierarchical community summarization and vector-based retrieval provide semantically organized knowledge augmentation, achieving recall rates of 0.719 and 0.694 on maintenance regulation queries and grading-based planning tasks, representing improvements of 2.36%～13.40% over mainstream LLM baselines. The framework consistently outperforms both non-RAG and conventional RAG configurations on complex domain-specific queries, demonstrating the effectiveness of structured semantic constraints and multi-hop reasoning in improving the professionalism and interpretability of generated responses. Despite these advances, the coupling mechanism between LLM reasoning and graph-structured inference remains only partially interpretable, limiting the transparency of the causal reasoning process from evidence nodes to maintenance decisions. Future research should therefore focus on enhancing causal reasoning within LLM-KG integration for safety-critical power system applications.

title: Identification de la biodiversité : la surveillance environnementale par l'apprentissage de réseaux de neurones graphement pensés
abstract: Dans notre époque d’avalanche de données, les capteurs qui les collectent se trouvent partout : ils sont dans les rues d’une métropole, sous l’eau ou sous une branche d’arbre hébergeant des espèces diverses. Soit pour détecter des voitures afin de sécuriser les milieux urbains, soit pour classifier des signaux sonores afin de préserver la santé des forêts, ce ne sont pas les données qui manquent, mais plutôt des spécialistes qui peuvent les analyser ou les labelliser, une tâche très chronophage qui nécessite parfois des compétences spécifiques. Aussi nécessaire que soit la surveillance de l’environnement, elle pose des enjeux éthiques comme celui de la protection de la vie privée. Une solution peut être trouvée en anonymisant toutes les données humaines permettant d’identifier les personnes, rendant possible l'utilisation de certains outils de surveillance en respectant ces normes éthiques. La question qui se pose est donc : comment le faire d’une façon à la fois rapide et fiable ? Ce sont les réseaux de neurones à graphes qui vont nous venir en aide. Grâce à leur structure, ces modèles mathématiques sont capables de relever automatiquement des connexions, ou des ressemblances parfois imperceptibles à l’œil non expérimenté, entre les données. Mieux encore, en passant par l’approche inductive, nous réussissons à diminuer le besoin de données labellisées.

title: Assessing the import of morphology in gender assignment: A computational study of French
abstract: En français, le genre grammatical d’un nom est influencé par l’interaction complexe d’indices sémantiques, phonologiques et morphologiques. Les études précédentes ont montré que le genre est partiellement prédictible à partir de la forme des mots, mais elles ne tranchent pas la question de savoir si la prédictibilité est principalement de source phonologique ou morphologique. Cet article aborde la question à l’aide de réseaux de neurones récurrents entraînés sur un grand lexique de noms du français. Nous évaluons des modèles entraînés sur des représentations orthographiques ou phonémiques, et examinons la qualité des prédictions et le déroulement de la prise de décision. Nos résultats montrent que le genre peut être prédit avec fiabilité à partir de la forme seule et que l’orthographe fournit des indices plus robustes que la phonologie. L’analyse d’erreur montre que le genre des noms non-construits est plus difficile à prédire que celui des noms suffixés. Crucialement, les prédictions les plus fiables et les plus consistantes résultent de séquences finales de mots correspondant le plus souvent à des suffixes dérivationnels. Ces résultats suggèrent que la morphologie est la cause ultime de la fiabilité de l’assignation du genre, alors que la forme de surface est l’intermédiaire par lequel cette prédictibilité émerge.

title: Scaling of English Intermediate-Task Performance Gains in Multilingual Model Transfer
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: Does the performance gain from English intermediate-task training for cross-lingual transfer scale with the size of the pretrained multilingual model when evaluated on XTREME NER and NLI tasks? title: Bipartite Epistemic Engine: Architecture, Thermodynamics, and the Kinetic Theory of the Knowledge Manifold
abstract: The full research program has been enormously productive in 2026. Early in the year Plasma Pareidolia and Adversarial Multi-model Orchestration (AMO) were published. A few additional papers were presented even if still in draft mode to share the concepts. There are far more concepts in the vault that are harder to communicate given the dependency stack. We've concluded implementation code which actually solves problems are a stronger approach than sharing research papers. The slides below introduce the engine being built at a very high level. The true scope is staggering as every system and subsystem mentioned here is dense with theory and implementation details. But the hope is that this will show the shape of what is being constructed. The theory is largely settled, all work is now pushed toward implementation software. We mark the beginning of 2H2026 optimistic in the direction this research is heading and will continue to share updates with anyone interested. The engine is being wired up. This work forms part of a broader research program examining how rendering, constraint, and convergence emerge in uncertain physical, cognitive, and social systems. title: Beyond Monolithic AI: A Federated Epistemic–Operational Architecture for Superadditive Cooperative Intelligence
abstract: Modern AI agents increasingly integrate perception, reasoning, planning, and action within a single monolithic architecture. Such designs can be highly capable, but they rarely provide explicit mechanisms for preserving uncertainty, governing changes to their own policies, or safely federating knowledge across agents. For safety-critical systems this is a serious gap: overconfidence, opaque decision-making, and unsafe coordination can each lead to catastrophic failure. We present the Federated Epistemic–Operational Architecture (FEOA), a constitutional design for building corrigible agents under uncertainty, and use it to introduce an architectural property we call Superadditive Cooperative Intelligence (SCI): capability that arises from governed cooperation rather than from scaling an individual model. FEOA separates agent behavior into three explicit layers — an epistemic belief substrate (Layer 1), an operational claim-acquisition layer (Layer 2), and a goal-directed action layer (Layer 3) — governed by a constitutional hierarchy in which Constitution outranks Policy, which outranks Action. Its central design principle is that cooperating agents exchange evidence rather than belief scores, which preserves each agent's local sovereignty while preventing the confidence corruption that repeated, correlated reports would otherwise cause. We validate the architecture with a dependency-free reference implementation and experiments spanning navigation and aerial-survey agents. The results show that FEOA resists false confidence under correlated-error conditions, and that heterogeneous agents cooperating across domains produce decisions that exist in no agent alone — a ground agent acting correctly on a hazard only an aerial agent could perceive. Together these results illustrate SCI: governed cooperation that makes each sovereign agent a more capable decision-maker than it could be alone — transforming the agents rather than merely pooling their outputs, and without sacrificing their sovereignty.

title: Surrogate-Model-Driven SMOTE: Learning to Generate Data via Adaptive Boundary-Aware Optimization
abstract: Class-imbalance is a pervasive and challenging issue in machine learning, where traditional classifiers often exhibit a strong bias towards the majority class. Although the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) and its variants mitigate this problem by interpolating between minority instances, their reliance on local geometric distances often introduces noisy samples into the majority class regions, leading to severe class overlapping and over-fitting. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a novel over-sampling framework named Surrogate-model SMOTE (SM-SMOTE), which introduces an efficient, differentiable surrogate model specifically trained to learn "how to generate high-quality data." Instead of performing blind random interpolation, SM-SMOTE leverages the surrogate model to perceive the global decision boundary and adaptively guide the sample generation process. We formulate the synthesis of new samples as a joint optimization problem that maximizes minority class confidence, captures boundary uncertainty, and applies regularization to preserve the original data manifold. By utilizing gradient flow directions, the initial candidate points are iteratively adjusted to find the optimal positions that expand the minority decision space without invading the majority class domain. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that SM-SMOTE effectively balances exploration and exploitation during data synthesis, substantially reducing negative transfer while enhancing the classifier's discriminative capability along complex boundaries.

title: Active Reset and Scheduling in Fault-Tolerant Quantum-Classical Cloud Computing
abstract: Quantum-classical cloud computing refers to a hybrid computing model that integrates quantum computing with classical computing resources, typically hosted on the cloud. The objective of this paper is threefold: First, to scrutinize the computing paradigm of quantum-classical cloud computing; second, to study the three pillars of the underpinning techniques: Active reset, scheduling, and fault tolerance; third, to demonstrate the realization of the aforementioned techniques. The active reset method leverages measurement and feedback to reset the qubit much faster and with high fidelity. The proposed scheduling algorithm is designed to efficiently manage quantum job execution in a fault-tolerant quantum-classical cloud computing environment. The paper also implements a Bayesian optimization process to optimize the hyper-parameters of a quantum error correction scheme. The research demonstrates significant performance gains across all three technical pillars of the hybrid cloud model. Specifically, the implementation of active reset reduced the qubit initialization time by 90 %, dropping from the 100 µs required for passive relaxation to just 10 µs while maintaining a high reset fidelity of 99.6 %. In terms of cloud resource management, the Shortest Job Next (SJN) scheduling algorithm drastically improved efficiency compared to FCFS, reducing peak wait times from 1.75 s to near-zero for many tasks. Furthermore, the application of Bayesian optimization to faulttolerant parameters successfully minimized the logical error rate from an initial 0.238 to 0.106, marking a 55 % improvement in the reliability of the quantum-classical computing environment.

title: Adopción e integración de inteligencia artificial en el proceso gerencial de toma de decisiones: un estudio exploratorio en empresas de servicios tecnológicos argentinas
abstract: La adopción de Inteligencia Artificial ha experimentado una aceleración sin precedentes desde 2022, pero persiste una brecha significativa entre el potencial tecnológico y el valor organizacional efectivamente capturado. Este estudio analiza la adopción e integración de herramientas de IA en los procesos gerenciales de toma de decisiones en empresas del sector de servicios tecnológicos en Argentina, explorando las percepciones directivas sobre los desafíos y oportunidades que presenta este fenómeno. La investigación adopta un diseño metodológico mixto que combina datos cuantitativos de 26 organizaciones mediante cuestionario estructurado con hallazgos cualitativos de seis entrevistas semiestructuradas con líderes empresariales. El análisis se estructura mediante un marco conceptual de cuatro niveles que examina el contexto sectorial, los factores organizativos, los procesos de adopción y los resultados capturados. Los hallazgos revelan que el sector se encuentra en una fase de adopción amplia pero predominantemente superficial. El 73% de las organizaciones utiliza herramientas de IA, con predominio de asistentes generativos (94.7% de usuarios), pero la integración permanece mayormente instrumental-táctica más que estratégica-transformadora. La penetración de IA es significativamente mayor en decisiones operativas que en estratégicas, con solo el 26% de los encuestados percibiendo mejoras en la objetividad de las decisiones. Los beneficios más reportados se concentran en eficiencia operativa: velocidad de análisis (73%), automatización de tareas (69%) e identificación de patrones (58%). evidence.title: Adopción e integración de inteligencia artificial en el proceso gerencial de toma de decisiones: un estudio exploratorio en empresas de servicios tecnológicos argentinas
evidence.abstract: La adopción de Inteligencia Artificial ha experimentado una aceleración sin precedentes desde 2022, pero persiste una brecha significativa entre el potencial tecnológico y el valor organizacional efectivamente capturado. title: Causal Discovery as Dialectical Aggregation: A Quantitative Argumentation Framework
abstract: Constraint-based causal discovery is brittle in finite-sample regimes because erroneous conditional-independence (CI) decisions can cascade into substantial structural errors. We propose Quantitative Argumentation for Causal Discovery (QACD), a semantics-driven framework that represents CI outcomes as graded, defeasible arguments rather than irreversible constraints. QACD maps statistical test outcomes to argument strengths and aggregates conflicting evidence through connectivity-mediated witness propagation, producing a fixed-point acceptability labeling over candidate adjacencies. Experiments on standard benchmark Bayesian networks suggest that QACD improves structural coherence and interventional reliability in several noisy or inconsistent CI regimes, while remaining competitive with classical constraint-based, hybrid, and prior argumentation-based baselines.

title: Decorrelated unbiased converted measurement Kalman filter for bistatic radar
abstract: Bistatic position measurements in radar systems are nonlinear functions of the Cartesian state. These nonlinearities pose challenges for many target tracking algorithms, leading to the well-known 'contact lens' effect, manifesting as nonlinear measurement artifacts in Cartesian coordinates. In monostatic radar, the CMKF (converted measurement Kalman filter) is commonly used to mitigate nonlinearities in measurements. However, the converted measurement model for bistatic radar lacks a closed-form expression, motivating our research to address this challenge. A track initiation technique for bistatic radar is developed, and the initial state is propagated and incorporated into the DUCM (decorrelated unbiased converted measurement) framework to reduce model complexity. The filter parameters of the proposed DUCM model parameters are derived through theoretical analysis, and the filtering steps are described. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior performance compared to other classical techniques.

title: Comprehensive guidelines for establishing sample diversity and data sufficiency in artificial intelligence diagnostic datasets for cervical liquid-based cytology
abstract: Liquid-based cytology (LBC) has become a core technology in cervical cancer screening, and artificial intelligence (AI) shows great potential in addressing issues such as the global shortage of cytopathologists and large variations in diagnostic results. However, the clinical reliability of AI systems in the field of cervical cytology fundamentally depends on the quality, diversity, and representativeness of their training and validation datasets. Drawing on evidence-based medicine principles, the latest research progress in China and globally, and clinical practices, these guidelines establish standardized requirements for sample diversity and data sufficiency in cervical LBC AI datasets to reduce algorithmic bias. The objective is to improve the real-world applicability of models and ensure their safe clinical application. This guideline strictly complies with standardized guideline development specifications, with transparent expert panel organization, systematic literature retrieval, standardized evidence grading, three-round Delphi expert consensus, external peer review, and dynamic update mechanisms. All quantitative threshold indicators in the recommendations are jointly formulated based on high-quality clinical evidence and expert consensus, with clear evidence sources and consensus construction processes to enhance the transparency, credibility, and operability of the guideline.

title: Quantum machine learning for object detection and segmentation: A comprehensive survey and future research directions
abstract: Small objects have become increasingly common in civil, industrial, and security sensitive environments, driving a strong demand for reliable vision-based detection and segmentation. While deep learning (DL) models have achieved impressive performance, their practicality is limited by the small sizes of objects, cluttered backgrounds, motion blur, domain shift, and the growing cost of training and inference. Quantum machine learning (QML) has recently emerged as a potential research direction for exploring alternative feature representations, optimization strategies, and learning paradigms under resource constrained conditions. However, its practical efficiency benefits for object detection and segmentation remain largely preliminary and context dependent. The literature on quantum methods for detection and segmentation is scattered across the QML, aerial vision, and remote sensing domains. We provide a structured review of quantum, hybrid quantum–classical (HQC), and quantum approaches for detection and segmentation. We classify existing methods based on four aspects: how features are encoded and represented in quantum systems, the use of quantum kernels, variational quantum circuits (VQC) for classification and detection, and quantum architectures combined with modern detection and segmentation models. We summarize the commonly used datasets for quantum techniques, evaluation protocols, and computational constraints, comparing the reported performance trends, scalability levels, and practical limitations of quantum-based methods. Finally, we identify the open challenges, including data-efficient learning, robustness to domain shift, and end-to-end quantum segmentation, along with the research directions relevant to bridging the gap between QML and real-world object perception systems.

title: BudgetBench: A Budget-Tiered Protocol and Pilot Harness for Memory Strategy Evaluation in Local Large Language Model Agents
abstract: For local large language model agents, active context is a scarce resource: memory capacity, prefill latency, cache growth, and service objectives all constrain how many input tokens each call can afford. We present BudgetBench, an active-budget protocol and reference harness that treats the per-call input-token budget as the independent variable when comparing memory strategies. Holding the model, task, sampler, and decoding fixed, it sweeps budgets over 2K, 4K, 8K, 16K, and 32K tokens and records quality, budget utilization, latency, and, as a first-class outcome, budget-violation rates. The core contribution is this reusable measurement surface: a swappable MemoryStrategy contract, explicit budget enforcement, deterministic or versioned graders, prompt-audit metadata, and reproducibility artifacts, released at https://github.com/aviskaar/budgetbench. We substantiate the protocol with pilot studies rather than final rankings. Across a local qwen2.5:1.5b pilot (89 items each on SWE-bench Verified and LongBench v2), a hosted 50-item Qwen3 30B-A3B LongBench replication with exact tokenization, and a 500-item LongMemEval oracle study scored by the official GPT-4o evaluator, the harness exposes budget-compliance failures, non-monotonic quality curves, and operating points that single-budget evaluation hides. The budgeted-versus-full-context direction remains unresolved: the local slice is near-null and the hosted replication favors full context in point estimate. We report results transparently, including that the early pilot's tokenizer approximation undercounts some served-model prompts, so its violation rows are tokenizer-approximation diagnostics, not claim-bearing results; all timings are operational diagnostics. The reusable contribution is the protocol, harness, and failure-reporting discipline needed to scale fixed-budget memory-strategy evaluation.

title: Multi-Objective Exploration and Preference Optimization via Mutual Information
abstract: Aligning large language models with diverse and heterogeneous human values requires multi-objective alignment methods to effectively trade off conflicting preference dimensions. Current methods achieve this trade-off by training policies conditioned on preference vectors and leveraging online direct preference optimization. However, exploration uncertainty can cause the reward distributions of responses generated under different preference vectors to overlap, and the generated responses may fail to effectively align with the corresponding preference vectors. In this paper, we propose Multi-Objective Exploration and Preference Optimization via Mutual Information (MI-EPO), an information-theoretic framework. It unifies multi-objective exploration and alignment by maximizing the joint conditional mutual information among generated responses, preference feedback, and preference vectors. By incorporating a probabilistic routing mechanism, MI-EPO naturally decomposes objective alignment and preference-aware exploration, encouraging the model to generate responses that are distinguishable and aligned with different preference conditions. Experiments on safe alignment and helpful assistant tasks show that MI-EPO significantly improves the alignment between generated responses and preference vectors, makes the outputs more controllable, and achieves stable trade-offs across multiple objectives.

title: Active Learning for Calibrating Entangling Gates via Surrogate-Based Optimization
abstract: The fidelity of a quantum gate is sensitive to small deviations in the physical control parameters. Unfortunately, it is generally difficult to exactly model the implemented Hamiltonian for a set of user-defined parameters, necessitating on-device calibration. Here, we present an active learning framework based on Bayesian optimization with a Gaussian Process surrogate to find the optimal parameter set. We validate the technique through numerical calibration of the laser amplitude and frequencies that implement the trapped-ion Mølmer Sørensen gate. We show that a Gaussian process can model the Hamiltonian dynamics. The addition of active learning accelerates the discovery of the optimal parameter set with speed and final fidelity dependent on the quantum projection noise of the data. These results establish the utility of active learning and surrogate models for quantum calibration and control.

title: Severity-Aware Curriculum Learning with Multi-Model Response Selection for Medical Text Generation
abstract: Telehealth systems have become increasingly important for delivering accessible and timely medical information. Existing large language models often struggle to provide consistent and contextually appropriate medical responses across varying levels of case severity. This limitation highlights the need for models that can effectively adapt to the progressive complexity in medical queries. To address this challenge, we introduce a severity-aware multi-model framework that integrates curriculum training strategy with relevance-based response selection. The proposed framework employs a three-stage curriculum learning strategy, where each model is trained sequentially on mild, moderate, and critical cases to progressively acquire domain knowledge. The approach uses five large language models, each trained independently under the same curriculum. During inference, all models generate candidate responses, and the response with highest BERTScore is selected as the final output. The framework is trained and evaluated on the MAQA dataset, which provides annotated medical question-answer pairs. Experimental results evaluated using BERTScore demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior performance compared to both baseline and fine-tuned models, attaining 86.71% in the baseline setting and 90.30% after fine-tuning. These results highlight the effectiveness of combining curriculum learning with multi-model response selection in improving response quality and relevance in medical text generation.

title: Utilizing Earth Foundation Models to Enhance the Simulation Performance of Hydrological Models with AlphaEarth Embeddings
abstract: Predicting river flow in places without streamflow records is challenging because basins respond differently to climate, terrain, vegetation, and soils. Traditional basin attributes describe some of these differences, but they cannot fully represent the complexity of natural environments. This study examines whether AlphaEarth Foundation embeddings, which are learned from large collections of satellite images rather than designed by experts, offer a more informative way to describe basin characteristics. These embeddings summarize patterns in vegetation, land surface properties, and long-term environmental dynamics. We find that models using them achieve higher accuracy when predicting flows in basins not used for training, suggesting that they capture key physical differences more effectively than traditional attributes. We further investigate how selecting appropriate donor basins influences prediction in ungauged regions. Similarity based on the embeddings helps identify basins with comparable environmental and hydrological behavior, improving performance, whereas adding many dissimilar basins can reduce accuracy. The results show that satellite-informed environmental representations can strengthen hydrological forecasting and support the development of models that adapt more easily to different landscapes.

title: Diseño e implementación de una secretaría digital basada en inteligencia artificial para la gestión automatizada de agendas y reuniones mediante interfaces conversacionales e integración con servicios en la nube
abstract: Este trabajo presenta el diseño e implementación de una secretaria digital basada en inteligencia artificial para automatizar la coordinación de reuniones entre estudiantes, docentes y personal administrativo de la Universidad Politécnica Salesiana, sede Cuenca, a través de WhatsApp. El sistema se desarrolló siguiendo Design-Based Research (DBR) combinado con SCRUM, sobre un backend en Python (FastAPI) que conecta WhatsApp mediante WAHA con Dify, plataforma que interpreta el lenguaje natural del usuario y orquesta las acciones del sistema. La lógica de disponibilidad, la negociación de horarios y la persistencia de la información se manejan en el backend, con los datos almacenados en Supabase; al confirmarse una reunión, el sistema crea automáticamente el evento en Google Calendar y genera un enlace de videollamada en Jitsi Meet.
